Generate full 256 color palette from the base16 palette

The theme builder now expands a validated base16 theme into a full
256-color ANSI palette at runtime.

Colors 16-231 are generated as a 6x6x6 cube using trilinear
interpolation in OKLab space, with cube corners anchored to
background/foreground and ANSI colors 1-6 (000=bg, 111=fg, and the other
six corners from ansi[1..6]). Colors 232-255 are generated as a
24-step grayscale ramp between background and foreground in OKLab.

Generated colors are converted back to #rrggbb; when a color is out of
sRGB gamut, chroma is reduced in OKLCH (binary search) to preserve
hue/lightness instead of RGB clipping.

This is heavily inspired by Jake Stewart's implementation presented in
his gist here: https://gist.github.com/jake-stewart/0a8ea46159a7da2c808e5be2177e1783

Our implementation differs from Jake's in the following ways:

- we do color interpolation in OKLAB instead of in CIELAB - OKLAB is
  more perceptually uniform

- we use OKLCH for gamut fallback instead of RGB clipping, as it
  preserves hue better and avoids "dirty" colors
